q: Markov triples (a,b,c) with a²+b²+c² = 3abc arise in Diophantine approximation. The Markov spectrum relates to the Lagrange spectrum of approximability of reals. Numbers with Markov constant m(α) ≥ √5 are related to:
opts: The 'worst-case' badly approximable numbers: those with CF partial quotients all equal to 1 (golden ratio, √5-related)
Periodic points of the doubling map
exp: Markov spectrum: isolated points below the Hall ray {m(α) < 3} correspond to Markov numbers. The least well-approximable numbers (largest m(α)) are related to the golden ratio: m((√5-1)/2) = √5. Periodic CF expansions with all 1s (quadratic irrationals related to φ) are hardest to approximate.
